import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    corr_threshold = 0.6
    correlated_pairs = set()
    
    # Identify correlated pairs
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(feats.ids):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(feats.ids[i+1:], i+1):
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:,i], feats.x[:,j])[0,1]) >= corr_threshold:
                correlated_pairs.add((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Select top features by t-statistic
    t_stats = []
    for fid in feats.ids:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, col_idx]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, col_idx]
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y1, y0, equal_var=False)
        t_stats.append(abs(t_stat))
    
    # Sort by t-statistic
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(t_stats)[::-1]
    top_features = [feats.ids[i] for i in sorted_indices[:20]]
    
    # Filter out near-duplicates
    selected_features = []
    for fid in top_features:
        is_duplicate = any(
            (fid, other) in correlated_pairs or (other, fid) in correlated_pairs
            for other in selected_features
        )
        if not is_duplicate:
            selected_features.append(fid)
    
    # Use only first few as drivers (max 4 to avoid exceeding limit)
    drivers = tuple(selected_features[:4])
    
    # For logistic regression, include all features with strong effect
    columns = tuple(selected_features[:10])
    
    # Check for potential interactions
    products = []
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(columns):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(columns[i+1:], i+1):
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:,feats.column(fid1)], 
                              feats.x[:,feats.column(fid2)])[0,1]) > 0.5:
                products.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(columns):
        idx = list(feats.ids).index(fid)
        loadings[fid] = float(t_stats[idx])
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
